subject.title: [Bug]: API keys can leak in error messages when a custom provider's base URL is unreachable

question: Should this credential-exposure issue be handled as a security-owned shared provider-error boundary before any automated repair is queued?
rationale: The source gap is real enough to keep open, but the fix touches credential handling across provider SDKs, transport errors, gateway events, and diagnostics, so maintainer/security intent should define the boundary first.

options.title: Security-owned shared boundary
options.body: Route the issue through security/provider maintainers, require a live repro or focused failing test, then implement one central sanitizer before provider errors are stored or broadcast.

options.title: Narrow provider patch
options.body: Patch only the obvious OpenAI-compatible error paths now, accepting the risk that other provider/runtime error surfaces remain inconsistent.

options.title: Keep gathering proof
options.body: Wait for a concrete live reproduction before assigning implementation, leaving the credential-exposure report open and labeled for security review.

recommendation.title: Security-owned shared boundary
recommendation.body: Route the issue through security/provider maintainers, require a live repro or focused failing test, then implement one central sanitizer before provider errors are stored or broadcast.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is tied to the current provider package layout and recent provider transport touches, making him the best available routing owner from the local history.
